takeaways: If a keyboard shortcut uses only a letter, number, punctuation or symbol key, people can turn it off, remap it to include a modifier such as Ctrl or Alt, or it only works while that component has focus.
Voice control users dictate words, which arrive as a stream of letters. Every letter can fire a single-key shortcut, so one spoken sentence can archive, delete or send things by accident.
Shortcuts like Ctrl+S or Alt+N are not covered. Shift does not count as a modifier here, because Shift plus a letter is still a letter.
Developers build the shortcuts. Designers decide which ones exist, where people turn them off or change them, and how they are listed.
failures: An email app where pressing “e” archives the open message, with no way to switch it off
A video player where “k” and “j” work anywhere on the page
A shortcuts list that cannot be edited or disabled
check: List every single-key shortcut in the product, including ones from third-party components.
For each, find the setting that turns it off or remaps it, or confirm it only works while its component has focus.
Check that the setting is easy to find, for example in Settings and in the shortcuts help panel.

quiz.question: A task app uses “d” to mark the selected task done, anywhere on the page. Which change meets 2.1.4?
options: Show the shortcut in a tooltip on the Done button
Add a setting to turn single-key shortcuts off, or change them to include Ctrl or Alt
quiz.why: A tooltip tells people the shortcut exists but does not stop accidental use. Shift+D is still just a letter key. Turning it off, or remapping it to include a modifier, stops voice users firing it by accident.

spec: List every single-key shortcut, what it does and where it is active.
Design the setting that turns shortcuts off or remaps them, and where it lives.
For shortcuts meant to work only inside a component, such as a player, note that they work only while it has focus.
review: What happens if someone dictates a sentence while this screen is open?
Could any of these shortcuts delete, send or archive something without a confirmation?
Where would someone go to turn these off?
tradeoff: Power users love single-key shortcuts because they are fast. Keep them, but add one switch in settings to turn them off or remap them, and scope player shortcuts to the player.
system: Register shortcuts in one place, so a single settings screen can list, remap and turn off all of them.
pitch: For someone using voice control, a single-key shortcut means one spoken word can delete their work. One settings toggle prevents it.
